safetyNotice.title: Safety Precaution
safetyNotice.description: Electrical items can be risky. If you're unsure, ask a professional before opening components.

repair.title: Repair
repair.subtitle: Inspect bulb, toggle switch, or cord contact
repair.defaultReason: Usually a bulb, plug or switch: low cost to check.
reasons: Low-cost diagnostic: In India, 80% of small appliance issues are a loose wire, blown fuse, or faulty switch (₹50–₹250 fix by a local electrician or DIY).
Zero waste footprint: keeps the entire fixture and cord out of the municipal landfill.
DIY beginner friendly: requires only a screwdriver and 15 minutes of calm focus.

cost.note: Testing with spare bulb is free; replacement switch, plug, or wire is ₹30–₹150.

effort.note: No delicate soldering or specialized workshop needed.

time.note: Diagnostic takes 5 minutes; part tightening under 15 minutes.

safety.note: Always unplug cord completely before inspecting contacts.

impact.note: Prevents manufacturing burden and keeps heavy materials in use.

repair.optimalCriteria: The bulb or switch is the root issue and body structure is intact. Wire casing shows no scorching.
toolsNeeded: Working replacement E26/E12 bulb or spare fuse
repair.communityTip: In older desk lamps, the socket contact brass tab flattens over time. With the lamp unplugged, gently lifting it 2mm with a clean pen often fixes it instantly!

checklists.text: 1. Unplug the item first
checklists.detail: Never inspect, touch electrical pins, or open base covers with the power cord plugged in.

checklists.text: 2. Swap in a known-good bulb or cable
checklists.detail: Test with a component known to work to rule out internal filament or driver burnout.

checklists.text: 3. Check the plug and cord for visible damage
checklists.detail: Inspect closely for crimped insulation, pet bites, or loose prongs near the outlet joint.

checklists.text: 4. Try a different wall socket
checklists.detail: Ensure the wall receptacle isn't connected to a tripped circuit breaker or wall switch.

repair.subsequentLabel: Still not working? Try Recycle next

householdFix.title: Household Contact & Switch Fix (Desi Jugaad)
householdFix.bestInexpensiveWay: Lift flattened brass socket contacts & clean oxidation using a pencil eraser or vinegar swab.
materialsNeeded: Pencil with rubber eraser or dry cotton earbud
Small drop of white vinegar or lemon juice (for oxidized prongs)
Screwdriver or dry butter knife tip
Spare bulb from another room to test
steps: Safety first: Unplug the appliance power cord completely from the wall socket before touching contacts.

Fix flattened contact tab: Over years of screwing bulbs or plugs in, the central brass contact tab flattens down. With the unit unplugged, gently lever the brass tab up by 2mm using a screwdriver or pen tip so it makes firm contact with the bulb base.
Clean oxidized terminals: 80% of intermittent failure is surface oxidation. Rub a clean pencil eraser over the metal prongs and internal contact points until the metal shines.
Check for loose cord screws: Open the 3-pin plug top and tighten the terminal screws holding the live, neutral, and earth wires firmly.
householdFix.safetyNotice: Always completely unplug the power cord from the wall socket before inspecting or touching electrical contacts.

recycle.title: Recycle
recycle.subtitle: Certified Municipal E-waste dropoff
recycle.defaultReason: Lamps and appliances are e-waste; use a proper drop-off.
reasons: Reclaims high-value metals like copper, brass, and aluminum rather than burying them.
Certified recyclers separate toxic solder traces away from soil and drinking water.
Zero cost at local council or household hazardous waste drop-off days.

cost.note: Municipal e-waste dropoff centers are free for residents.

effort.note: Requires batching with your next weekend recycling trip.

time.note: Transit and drop-off window at nearby depot.

safety.note: Keep glass shades intact when transporting.

impact.note: Metals and polymers are shredded and returned to manufacturing.

recycle.optimalCriteria: The internal transformer or unibody casing is burnt, broken beyond simple part swap, or unsafe.
toolsNeeded: Cardboard box or bag for safe transit
recycle.communityTip: Most hardware stores and municipal depots host free e-waste collection bins near the entrance.

checklists.text: 1. Remove detachable bulbs or batteries
checklists.detail: Separate mercury fluorescent bulbs or lithium batteries for dedicated sorting bins.

checklists.text: 2. Wind and secure the electrical cord
checklists.detail: Wrap the cord loosely around the base so it doesn't tangle in transport.

checklists.text: 3. Locate your nearest e-waste drop-off bin
checklists.detail: Search your local city recycling directory or electronics retailer collection point.

repurpose.subtitle: Convert shade or weighted base creatively

safetyNotice.title: Ergonomic & Structural Safety
safetyNotice.description: Ensure weight-bearing joints and fasteners are tightened securely before sitting.

repair.title: Repair
repair.subtitle: Tighten bolts, regue joints, or swap cylinder
repair.defaultReason: Most loose joints and sinking cylinders can be secured in 20 minutes.
reasons: Local hardware store bolts or Fevicol wood glue cost under ₹50–₹100 and restore full structural strength.
Office chair hydraulic gas-lift cylinders can be replaced for ₹450–₹750 from local hardware markets or online.
Preserves seasoned wood or quality steel frames that outlast cheap modern flat-pack.

cost.note: Fevicol/screws (₹50–₹100) or universal hydraulic gas-lift cylinder (₹450–₹650).

effort.note: Simple hand tools like an Allen key or mallet.

time.note: Straightforward bolt tightening or clamp installation.

safety.note: Watch fingers around scissor joints and springs.

impact.note: Keeps 10–25 kg of bulky furniture out of landfills.

repair.optimalCriteria: Frame structure is solid; issue is loose bolts, sinking gas strut, or dry glue joints.
toolsNeeded: PVA wood glue or cylinder clamp kit
repair.communityTip: For an office chair that sinks, a ₹30–₹50 jubilee hose clamp from a local hardware store tightened around the silver cylinder shaft permanently locks it at your preferred height!

checklists.text: 1. Flip item onto a rug or towel
checklists.detail: Protect the floor and get clear visual access to all underside bolts.

checklists.text: 2. Hand-tighten all connecting bolts
checklists.detail: Go diagonally across bolts to ensure even alignment across the frame.

checklists.text: 3. Add locking washers or wood glue to threads
checklists.detail: Prevents vibration and body weight from loosening screws over time.

repair.subsequentLabel: Still unsteady? Repurpose for garden or storage

householdFix.title: Jubilee Clamp Cylinder Lock & Toothpick Screw Fix
householdFix.bestInexpensiveWay: Lock a sinking office chair with a ₹30 hardware jubilee clamp, or repair loose wobbly screw holes with wooden toothpicks and Fevicol.
materialsNeeded: ₹30 jubilee hose clamp from local hardware store (lohe ki dukaan)
Wooden toothpicks or matchsticks
Fevicol or household glue
Screwdriver or Allen key
steps: For a sinking office chair: Pull the chair up to your favorite height. Slide the plastic telescopic cover up to expose the silver metal cylinder. Wrap a ₹30 jubilee metal hose clamp around the top of the silver shaft and tighten the bolt firmly with a screwdriver. The clamp acts as a physical mechanical stop that permanently locks the chair at your height without sinking!
For loose screws & stripped screw holes: Remove the loose screw. Dip 2–3 wooden toothpicks or matchsticks into Fevicol, jam them into the stripped hole, and snap them off flush with the surface.
Drive the screw back in: The wooden toothpicks compress and give the screw threads solid new wood grain to bite into, creating a rock-solid tight fit.
For water marks or surface scuffs: Mix a drop of mustard/cooking oil with a pinch of fine salt, rub gently with a soft cloth over surface rings, and buff dry.
householdFix.safetyNotice: Never attempt to puncture or drill into pneumatic gas lift cylinders as they contain pressurized gas.

householdFix.title: Pencil-Graphite Zipper Fix & Desi Darzi Seam Stitch
householdFix.bestInexpensiveWay: Lubricate stuck zippers instantly with a graphite pencil or soap bar, and secure unraveling seams with clear nail polish or a simple backstitch.
materialsNeeded: Standard HB or 2B graphite pencil or dry bar soap
Sewing needle and thread (₹15 spool)
Clear nail polish (to stop unraveling threads)
Safety pin or paperclip (emergency zipper pull)
steps: For stuck or stubborn zippers: Rub the tip of an ordinary graphite pencil or a dry cake of bath soap along both sides of the zipper teeth. Graphite is a natural dry lubricant that allows teeth to glide effortlessly without staining fabric.
For a broken zipper pull tab: Thread a small safety pin, paperclip, or key ring through the zipper slider loop for an immediate, heavy-duty pull tab.
For torn seams or split hems: Turn garment inside out, align edges, and use a tight needle backstitch (each stitch overlaps the previous one) 3mm inside the raw edge for machine-grade durability.
Stop frayed edges: Dab a tiny drop of clear nail polish or fabric adhesive along frayed fabric raw edges to seal fibers instantly.
householdFix.safetyNotice: Use a coin or thimble when pushing needles through thick denim seams to avoid finger pricks.

Cotton cloth or sandpaper to clean surface
repair.communityTip: Before gluing a peeling sole, clean both surfaces with rubbing alcohol and roughen with sandpaper. Clamp with rubber bands overnight for a permanent bond!

checklists.text: 1. Clean and dry the bonding surfaces
checklists.detail: Wipe dirt and grease away with rubbing alcohol or soapy water and dry completely.

checklists.text: 2. Apply flexible polyurethane shoe glue

checklists.text: 3. Secure under pressure for 24 hours
checklists.detail: Wrap tight with rubber bands or weigh down with a heavy book.

householdFix.title: Pliers Zipper Clamp & Fevikwik + Baking Soda Sole Fix
householdFix.bestInexpensiveWay: Gently squeeze loose zipper slider jaws with pliers in 10 seconds to fix separated teeth, or bond peeling soles with Fevicol ShoeFix / Fevikwik.
materialsNeeded: Household pliers
Fevicol ShoeFix (₹35) or Fevikwik (₹10)
Pinch of baking soda (for instant plastic weld)
Heavy rubber bands or heavy books (for clamping)
Old toothbrush & sandpaper (to clean bonding surface)
steps: For separated zippers (teeth open behind slider): When bag or shoe zippers pull apart, the metal slider jaws have spread open. Take ordinary pliers and gently squeeze the sides of the slider top-and-bottom by 1mm. This re-aligns the teeth and fixes 90% of split zippers in 10 seconds!
For peeling shoe/sandal soles: Roughen both the rubber sole and shoe base with sandpaper. Clean off grit with a dry cloth.
Apply shoe adhesive: Spread a thin, even coat of Fevicol ShoeFix on both surfaces. Wait 2 minutes for slight tackiness, then press firmly together.

Instant acrylic plastic weld: For cracked plastic buckles, heel tabs, or eyelets, put a drop of Fevikwik and immediately sprinkle a pinch of baking soda over it. It creates an instant stone-hard acrylic polymer bridge!
Clamp overnight: Wrap tightly with rubber bands or place under heavy books for 12 hours.
householdFix.safetyNotice: Avoid skin contact with Fevikwik; keep away from eyes.

householdFix.title: Baking Soda Odor Strip & Cookware Threadlocker Fix
householdFix.bestInexpensiveWay: Lock loose pan handles with nail polish on screw threads, and strip turmeric curry stains from plastic using baking soda and sunlight.
materialsNeeded: Baking soda (meetha soda) & warm water
Clear nail polish (budget threadlocker)
Phillips screwdriver
400-grit wet sandpaper (for smoothing ceramic chips)
steps: For loose cookware handles: Unscrew the handle screw completely. Coat the screw threads with a drop of clear nail polish (acts as a vibration-proof threadlocker), re-insert into the handle, and tighten firmly with a screwdriver. It prevents the screw from loosening from heat cycles.

For stained or smelly plastic containers: Make a thick paste of 2 tablespoons baking soda and warm water. Coat the inside, place the open container in direct sunlight for 3–4 hours, then rinse. Sunlight and baking soda break down tough turmeric and oil stains.
For leaking flask or bottle lids: Remove the silicone rubber gasket ring, wash thoroughly, turn it upside down, and re-fit it into the lid groove. The reverse side creates an airtight new seal.
For chipped ceramic mug bottoms (non-food surface): Smooth the rough chip with wet sandpaper to prevent scratching tables or hurting hands.
householdFix.safetyNotice: Never use chemical industrial glues on surfaces that come into direct contact with boiling food or hot liquids.

householdFix.title: Fevikwik + Baking Soda Super-Bridge & Battery Contact Clean
householdFix.bestInexpensiveWay: Reinforce snapped plastic brackets with Fevikwik + baking soda composite, and clean corroded battery contacts with a vinegar-dipped earbud.
materialsNeeded: Fevikwik (₹10 tube)
Household baking soda (meetha soda from kitchen)
Cotton earbud / swab with a drop of vinegar or lemon juice
Rubber band or aluminum foil strip (for stripped screw grip)
steps: For corroded battery contacts: If an item or gadget won't turn on, inspect the battery springs for white/green corrosion. Dip a cotton earbud in vinegar or lemon juice and rub the springs until the shiny metal reappears. Dry completely before inserting fresh batteries.

Super-strong plastic bond: For cracked or snapped plastic parts, hold the joint together, apply a line of Fevikwik, and immediately dust it with baking soda. The chemical reaction forms an instant, drillable, stone-hard plastic weld that is 5x stronger than glue alone.
For stripped screw holes in plastic: Lay a small piece of rubber band or folded aluminum foil over the hole and drive the screw in. The rubber/foil fills the void and provides instant friction grip.
For stuck hinges or squeaky joints: Apply one drop of coconut or machine oil to the pivot pin and flex it back and forth several times.
householdFix.safetyNotice: Always disconnect batteries or power sources before cleaning internal contacts.
